newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian king asks Khmer Rouge about missing Briton.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian king asks Khmer Rouge about missing Briton.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk has asked Khmer Rouge leader Khieu Samphan for information on the fate and whereabouts of a British mine clearance expert abducted by armed men more than six months ago.

Sihanouk, in a letter to Khieu Samphan dated Saturday and released by the palace on Sunday, said Christopher Howes and his interpreter Houn Hourth were believed to be held in the northern region of Anlong Veng, held by hardline Khmer Rouge forces.

"I would be very grateful, excellency, if you would launch an enquiry so that all light can be shed on this incident and their liberation be secured as soon as possible," he wrote in the letter, addressed to Khieu Samphan through an associate in Paris.
Armed men abducted Howes, a mine clearance supervisor with the British-based Mines Advisory Group (MAG), and Houn Hourth in the northwest province of Siem Reap in late March.

Conflicting accounts of their whereabouts and captors emerged over the following weeks but the government finally asserted they had been moved north to the Anlong Veng stronghold of one-legged Khmer Rouge commander Ta Mok.
The Bangkok Post in late August cited an unidentified source on the Thai-Cambodian border as saying Howes and his colleague were dead.
But Khmer Rouge defectors told reporters in the northwest town of Sisophon on October 20 that the two men were still alive and Howes was helping the hardliners produce landmines.
The Khmer Rouge, whose 1975-79 rule left more than one million people dead, have been fighting the government since reneging on a 1991 peace pact and boycotting U.N.-run elections in 1993.
The Maoist group has kidnapped more than dozen westerners since the coalition government was formed in 1993 and killed at least seven of them.
A major split in the Khmer Rouge in August and the defections of thousands of guerrillas to the government in the past month has raised hopes for a happy ending to the Howes kidnap case.
